profiles.summary: The second backend behind forno.celo.org is now tied to source: it is celo-org/op-geth commit c7ed55b8, built on go-ethereum v1.16.9 with holiman/uint256 v1.3.2, and its instruction, jump table, jump destination, memory and stack files are byte identical to go-ethereum v1.16.9. Pinned to that backend, the battery, the targeted vectors, the call semantics words, the slot reads and the first script set match the specification and Ethereum. The celo-reth backend is unchanged at reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb.

deltas.delta: The version string Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 names celo-org/op-geth commit c7ed55b8. At that commit version/version.go sets the upstream version to 1.16.9 stable and the op-geth version to 0.1.0 untagged, and go.mod pins github.com/holiman/uint256 v1.3.2.

core/vm/instructions.go, jump_table.go, analysis_legacy.go, jumpdests.go, memory.go, memory_table.go, stack.go, common.go, eips.go and operations_acl.go at celo-org/op-geth c7ed55b8 are byte identical to go-ethereum v1.16.9. The fork changes only the precompile lookup (Celo transfer precompile at 0xfd and the OP precompile sets), an optional caller override and code size switch used by tooling, and always calls SetCode after a create, including for empty code.

forno.celo.org routes by method. In 120 three-item batches, eth_getStorageAt and eth_getCode went to celo-reth 40 times out of 40 each, while eth_getBlockByNumber went to the op-geth backend 8 times out of 40. eth_call batches reached op-geth on about one batch in six. Both backends returned block hash 0xd4da1293...98e6 and state root 0x17c4f200...091c for block 83,640,000.
deltas.source: https://forno.celo.org batched web3_clientVersion with eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_getStorageAt and eth_getCode at block 0x4fc3ec0, 2026-11-24

deltas.delta: celo-kona main now locks revm-interpreter 42.0.0, ruint 1.20.0 and alloy-primitives 1.7.3. No celo-reth release after v1.0.10 (20 November 2026) exists, and v1.0.10 only patches revm tracing of a duplicated SELFDESTRUCT transfer.

profiles.summary: Pinned to the op-geth backend, 12,198 storage and transient slot reads through the PoolManager's extsload and exttload paths give no alias, and the 50 call semantics words match. The two backends agree on block hash and state root. Nothing new on transaction boundaries.

Nothing new on the gas token. Karst, which Celo plans for Q4 2026 without a date, would cap a transaction at 16,777,216 gas under EIP-7825; this limits the length of a single swap loop for the sender only.

deltas.delta: Celo's H2 2026 roadmap names Karst as the next hardfork, planned for Q4 2026 pending implementation readiness, with no date. Karst on the OP Stack includes EIP-7825 (transaction gas cap), EIP-7823 and EIP-7883 (MODEXP bounds and pricing), EIP-7951 (P256 gas), EIP-7939 (CLZ) and a lower bn256 pairing input cap.

profiles.summary: The op-geth backend's transfer precompile at 0xfd has the same guards as celo-reth: it fails in static context, for any caller other than the CELO token and for input other than 96 bytes, and checks the balance before moving value.

deltas.delta: celo-org/op-geth c7ed55b8 core/vm/celo_contracts.go: transfer.Run returns ErrWriteProtection when readOnly is set, refuses callers other than the CeloToken address from the chain's address registry, requires 96 bytes of input, warms both addresses after Jovian and fails with ErrInsufficientBalance before Transfer.

profiles.summary: The endpoint still reports reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7 and no xlayer-reth release followed v0.0.7.3-rc.1. Its lock takes revm 40.0.3, revm-interpreter 37.0.3 and revm-bytecode 11.0.1 from crates.io and ruint 1.18.0, which is above the patched range of RUSTSEC-2025-0137. 3,010 new mined swaps replay to the unit.

deltas.delta: xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 Cargo.lock: revm 40.0.3, revm-interpreter 37.0.3, revm-bytecode 11.0.1, revm-handler 20.0.3, revm-context 18.0.3 and ruint 1.18.0 come from the crates.io registry; op-revm 20.0.0 and alloy-op-evm 0.32.0 come from the okx/optimism fork (no registry source), which holds the gasless handler changes read in cycle 11.
RUSTSEC-2025-0137 (unsound reciprocal_mg10 with debug-only bounds checks) affects ruint below 1.17.0 and is patched from 1.17.1. X Layer's 1.18.0 and Celo's 1.20.0 are outside it.

The xlayer-reth releases page lists v0.0.7.3-rc.1 (5 November) as the newest release. The chain spec on main still ends at Jovian (mainnet timestamp 1764691201) with no Karst or Osaka entry, so no X Layer execution fork is scheduled in the public code.

profiles.summary: Nothing new. The gasless system call and the reth execution cache were read in cycles 11 and 14.
Nothing new on OKB as gas token or on the gasless whitelist.
Nothing new. No new advisory or release touches the predeploys or precompiles.

findings.title: Base and Celo block builders read through the reth execution cache that still has the stale branch for a destroyed account without code, when the operator enables cache sharing
findings.difference: Celo's endpoint still reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, the celo-org/reth revision with the old insert_state branch for a destroyed account whose original info had no code. The block builder reads through the execution cache only when the engine is started with --engine.share-execution-cache-with-payload-builder, whose default is false.
findings.mechanism: 1. Nothing about the code path changed since cycle 14: the endpoint reports the same build and celo-reth v1.0.10 only patched tracing. 2. The public node setup that Celo publishes starts celo-reth without the sharing flag, so follower and RPC nodes built from it never hand the cache to a builder. The sequencer's own start parameters are not published. 3. The PoolManager's storage is never on the faulty branch, because it has code from deployment and cannot be destroyed, and transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) is not cached across transactions. Only a contract created in the block that destroyed its codeless address can read a stale word, so only an attacker-made token or hook could be affected, and such a contract can misreport balances to sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) without any cache fault.
findings.impact: No funds held by the PoolManager for other users move. If the flag is on at the sequencer and the trigger works, unsafe blocks could be published with a state that followers reject, and swaps and liquidity changes in them would be re-executed after the reorg.
findings.preconditions: The Celo sequencer operator runs with cache sharing enabled, and some read in an ordinary block caches a word for a codeless address that a later transaction in the block destroys and re-creates. Neither link is confirmed.
findings.mitigations: Celo upgrades celo-org/reth to a revision with the reth pull request 28148 fix, or keeps sharing off. Integrators wait for safe or finalized blocks before treating a fill as final.

sources.supports: v1.0.10 of 20 November is the newest celo-reth release and only fixes SELFDESTRUCT tracing
the published node start script runs celo-reth without --engine.share-execution-cache-with-payload-builder

findings.title: X Layer block builder can exclude PoolManager transactions through a rule driven risk control filter, which leaves L1 deposits as the exit
findings.difference: The X Layer execution client that every mainnet node runs contains a risk control filter in the block builder. It is off by default and needs a service URL. No release after v0.0.7.3-rc.1 changed it.
findings.mechanism: 1. Every PoolManager exit is a take inside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 291-297), which the sequencer has to include. 2. With the filter on, a rule from the external service can deny or hold a transaction, and the per-transaction capture limits deny a transaction whose simulation exceeds them. 3. The release page lists v0.0.7.3-rc.1 as the newest release, and the release notes still say nothing about whether the mainnet sequencer enables the filter. No OKX statement on the sequencer setting was found in this cycle. 4. L1 deposits are outside the builder filter.
findings.impact: While a matching rule is active, users cannot exit the affected pools through sequencer transactions. No funds are lost and the code in src/ has no time dependence.
findings.preconditions: The sequencer operator enables the filter and the risk control service delivers a rule that matches PoolManager activity. Neither is confirmed.
findings.mitigations: Keep an EOA controlled path for positions so that an L1 deposit can reach them, and ask OKX to state whether the filter runs on mainnet.

sources.supports: v0.0.7 added the Risk Control Service transaction filter; v0.0.7.3-rc.1 is the newest release and its notes do not mention the filter's mainnet state
the endpoint still reports reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7

cleared.check: Opcode battery (99,985 vectors) and targeted vectors (85,544) on the op-geth backend of forno.celo.org, pinned by sending each eth_call between two web3_clientVersion requests in one batch and keeping only answers where both name Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8.
cleared.result: Battery: 99,985 of 99,985 as specified, 167 batches kept on op-geth and 901 discarded as reth. Targeted: 85,544 of 85,544 as specified, 143 batches kept on op-geth, 714 discarded as reth, and no batch mixed the two backends.

cleared.check: Call semantics (callsem.py, 50 words) and storage and transient slot reads (statekeys.py, 6,099 storage and 6,099 transient reads) on the pinned op-geth backend.
cleared.result: 50 of 50 words as specified, and no slot alias in either storage kind. The rules that settlement rests on (revert undoes transient and persistent writes, static calls cannot write, return data size and copy bounds, value moves exactly) hold on op-geth as on celo-reth.

cleared.check: First PoolManager script set (pmdiff.py, 250 scripts, 12,322 PoolManager calls) on the pinned op-geth backend against Ethereum.
cleared.result: All 250 scripts return the same bytes as Ethereum (250 batches kept on op-geth, 1,299 discarded as reth). The Ethereum reference ran 11,892 calls, 667 of them reverting, across initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap, donate, mint, burn, take, clear, settle and extsload.

cleared.check: Source of the op-geth backend's interpreter: does celo-org/op-geth c7ed55b8 change any instruction, the jump destination analysis, memory or stack handling relative to go-ethereum v1.16.9.
cleared.result: instructions.go, jump_table.go, analysis_legacy.go, jumpdests.go, memory.go, memory_table.go, stack.go, common.go, eips.go and operations_acl.go are byte identical to go-ethereum v1.16.9. The integer library is holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. The differences in evm.go and interpreter.go concern precompile lookup, a tooling caller override and code size switches that are off in a node, and SetCode for empty created code, none of which reaches MULMOD, DIV, shifts, SIGNEXTEND, KECCAK256 or JUMPI used by src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and 48, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:12-45 or the swap loop at src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-352.

cleared.check: Do the two forno backends agree on chain state today.
cleared.result: Both returned block hash 0xd4da12937e3ef4c18ab945362bf3ca4590dee276009dcd6fdf324f08610698e6 and state root 0x17c4f200ec7971742895c7817d1e0eeddbeea3adc93c8a3e11ab7579625b091c for block 83,640,000. eth_getStorageAt and eth_getCode are always served by celo-reth, so direct state reads by integrators never hit op-geth.
cleared.source: https://forno.celo.org batched web3_clientVersion with eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_getStorageAt and eth_getCode at block 0x4fc3ec0, 2026-11-24

cleared.check: Mined swaps on X Layer replayed with replay2.py: 3,010 swaps in blocks 76,770,108 to 76,776,617.
cleared.result: All 3,010 satisfy the tick relation; 2,974 match one step of SwapMath.computeSwapStep and the other 36 match through the whole loop of Pool.swap (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437); none unmatched. 33 static fees match slot0 and 28 of 28 feeGrowthGlobal changes match.

cleared.check: Mined swaps on Celo replayed with replay2.py in blocks 83,104,894 to 83,644,893.
cleared.result: 428 swaps; all satisfy the tick relation, 370 match one step and 58 match through the whole loop, up to 46 steps; 58 static fees and 40 feeGrowthGlobal changes match. The window could not be widened: the tool stops at this range on forno, which caps eth_getLogs at 5,000 blocks, and the Celo PoolManager emits only a few logs per 5,000 blocks.

cleared.check: Karst CLZ opcode (0x1e, EIP-7939): does the PoolManager bytecode contain the byte as an instruction, which would turn a reachable invalid opcode into a valid one after the fork.
cleared.result: A linear disassembly of the 24,009 byte runtime built from this checkout (build/PoolManager.json) has no 0x1e instruction outside push data, and no CREATE, CREATE2, SELFDESTRUCT, BLOBHASH or BLOBBASEFEE. The fork does not change what the bytecode executes.

cleared.check: Karst transaction gas cap of EIP-7825 on Celo: can it leave someone unable to withdraw.
cleared.result: Removing liquidity touches two ticks and one position (PoolManager.modifyLiquidity at src/PoolManager.sol:145) and take and burn are constant cost, so a withdrawal fits far below 16,777,216 gas. Only a swap loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344) can grow with the ticks it crosses, and its sender can split it with a price limit. The cap affects only the sender's own transaction.

cleared.check: ruint advisories other than RUSTSEC-2026-0220 that could reach X Layer's ruint 1.18.0.
cleared.result: The only other ruint advisory, RUSTSEC-2025-0137, affects versions below 1.17.0 and is patched from 1.17.1. 1.18.0 is outside it.

cleared.check: Transfer precompile 0xfd on the op-geth backend: can a PoolManager native payout or settle on op-geth move CELO differently from celo-reth.
cleared.result: The precompile refuses any caller other than the CELO token and fails in static context, so a call from the PoolManager at src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 reverts on both clients. The guards match the celo-reth reading of cycle 11.

leads.question: When a celo-reth release ships revm-interpreter 42.0.0 from celo-kona main, does it turn on keccak-cache-global, and do the battery, targeted vectors and script sets still pass on its celo-reth backend?
leads.why: It replaces the interpreter crate of Celo's only block producer.

leads.question: Extend the Celo mined-swap window beyond blocks 83,104,894 to 83,644,893 with a log scanner that steps 5,000 blocks at a time back to the PoolManager's deployment, then replay with replay2.py.
leads.why: Celo stays the thinnest mined-swap window, and replay2.py stops at this range on forno.

leadResults.answer: The build is celo-org/op-geth commit c7ed55b8 on go-ethereum v1.16.9 with holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. Its interpreter, jump analysis, memory and stack files equal go-ethereum v1.16.9 byte for byte. Requests were pinned to it by batching each call between two web3_clientVersion requests: no batch was served by two backends. On op-geth, callsem (50 of 50), statekeys (12,198 reads, no alias), targeted (85,544, no mismatch), battery (99,985, no mismatch) and pmdiff (250 of 250 scripts identical to Ethereum) all match. forno routes eth_getStorageAt and eth_getCode only to celo-reth.

Operator level. Celo's published node start script does not set --engine.share-execution-cache-with-payload-builder, but the sequencer's flags and its standby setup are not public. F-132 is re-reported for Celo without change of severity.

No celo-reth release has been tagged from main since v1.0.10 of 20 November 2026, which keeps revm-interpreter 35.0.1. celo-kona main locks revm-interpreter 42.0.0 with ruint 1.20.0 and alloy-primitives 1.7.3. The lead stays open as a lower priority lead in this file.
Operator level. No deployment file or OKX statement on the mainnet sequencer's rcs-filter setting was found; v0.0.7.3-rc.1 is still the newest release. F-024 is re-reported unchanged.

Celo: replay2.py gives 428 swaps in blocks 83,104,894 to 83,644,893, all matched, and does not extend further on forno, which caps eth_getLogs at 5,000 blocks and holds few PoolManager logs per range. A new lead asks for a stepwise scanner. World Chain is outside this unit. X Layer was extended as well: 3,010 swaps, all matched.

Not traced in this cycle. Whatever the read, the faulty branch cannot reach the PoolManager's storage or that of contracts a victim pool already uses, as F-132 states, so the lead only bears on operator level liveness on Celo and X Layer.
